findings.area: enforcement strength — registry classification silences the checker without verifying the file
findings.finding: `check-no-competing-guides.mjs` treats `program/guide-registry.v1.json` as ground truth about a file's disposition rather than verifying the file's actual content. Control flow: DEMOTING_HEADERS match → `continue`; else no ACTIVE_MARKERS → `continue`; else registry lookup — and a finding is raised ONLY when `entry.classification === "active-implementation-guidance"`. Consequently, reclassifying a file in the registry to `historical-evidence` or `product-local-operational-doc` permanently silences the checker for that file whether or not the demoting header was ever written. The six demotions the refactor performed are uncommitted working-tree edits (43 insertions, 0 deletions, branch `refactor/competing-guide-dispositions`) that HANDOFF.md:148-152 explicitly offers the user to "take or leave". If the user declines them, the registry still records the demoted classification and the check still passes — the estate would assert compliance it does not have. The same weakness means a later regression that strips a demoting header is undetectable.
findings.evidence: `/home/heathledger/Documents/ioi/impl-refactor/checkout/internal-docs/implementation/tools/check-no-competing-guides.mjs:131-160`: `const hits = ACTIVE_MARKERS.filter(...); if (hits.length === 0) continue; const entry = classified.get(rel); if (!entry) { error } ... if (entry.classification === "active-implementation-guidance") { finding }` — no branch verifies that a demoted file carries a demoting header. `git status --porcelain` in the checkout shows the 6 demotions as unstaged modifications (` M apps/hypervisor/AGENTS.md`, etc.); `git diff --stat` = "6 files changed, 43 insertions(+)".
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `demotion_applied` bar: for every registry entry whose disposition is `reclassify-header-applied` or `reclassify-header-only`, assert the file actually matches a DEMOTING_HEADERS pattern in its first 4000 bytes; error when it does not. findings.finding: A single `certify-stage <STAGE> --no-run` writes a PASS certification with zero focused checks; every subsequent full run reuses it and executes none of the stage's declared checks. Independently, the input digest covers only the stage definition, that stage's own records, and the module file — not the repository source the focused checks exercise, and not children belonging to other stages. So a stage stays certified after the implementation regresses.
findings.evidence: Executed: `certify-stage.mjs FUTURE --no-run` → `PASS`, wrote `generated/.certify/FUTURE.ba2494b0bd1591e0.json`. Immediately after, `certify-stage.mjs FUTURE` (full run) → `inputs unchanged; reusing cached certification FUTURE.ba2494b0bd1591e0.json` / `0 focused check(s)`, while stages/future.md declares 10 focused checks. Mechanism: tools/certify-stage.mjs:195 gates checks on `!fs.existsSync(cachePath)`; :248-250 writes the cache on any PASS regardless of whether checks ran; :175-185 builds the digest from `stage`, `mine` (records with `stage_id === stageId`) and the module sha only. Header comment line 19 — "a stale cache cannot certify a changed stage" — is false in both directions.
findings.suggested_fix: Never write the cache when `--no-run` was passed or when `checks.length === 0` while the module declares commands; include a repo tree digest (or at least the git HEAD + dirty state) and every named child's record digest in the input digest.

findings.area: certify-stage — child literal check silently passes when its input is missing
findings.finding: A child record that declares no literal exit is skipped, not failed. Combined with the field mismatch above, the header's claim that certify-stage "checks every child's retained literal exit is present exactly once in an artifact whose digest matches" is satisfied vacuously for every child in the estate. On `--apply` the aggregate is then bound to `literals[0]` — one arbitrary child's literal — and its adversarial gate is satisfied by the aggregate's own self-declared prose.
findings.evidence: tools/certify-stage.mjs:139 `if (!literal) continue;`. tools/certify-stage.mjs:261 `literal_exit: literals[0] ?? null`. tools/certify-stage.mjs:262 `adversarial_or_fault_proof: aggregate.adversarial_or_fault_proof ?? []` — the record vouches for itself, and transition.mjs:146 only tests that the array is non-empty.
findings.suggested_fix: Make a missing literal an error for any child claiming `verified`; require the aggregate's proof to reference every child literal, not `literals[0]`.

findings.area: atomicity — the transaction is not atomic after the commit point
findings.finding: The claim "every file is staged in memory, the whole set is validated, and nothing is written unless all of it holds" covers only the validation phase. After the two record writes land, four external regenerations run with no try/catch and no rollback. Any nonzero exit throws an unhandled exception with the status already flipped on disk.
findings.evidence: tools/transition.mjs:193 flushes the writes; :196-205 then runs `refresh-canon-snapshots --write`, `canon-impact --write`, `sort-work-items --write`, `generate-now --write` via `run()` (execFileSync, which throws on nonzero). Exact failure window: transition.mjs:193 → :205. A failure at :200 leaves the record `verified`, evidence registered, canon snapshots refreshed, but canon-impact, work-item filing and NOW.md/program-state stale. `sort-work-items --write` (tools/sort-work-items.mjs:42-46) does `fs.renameSync` per record, so a crash mid-loop leaves records split across active/ and proposed/. A second, earlier window exists at transition.mjs:193 itself: the two `writeJsonDeterministic` calls are sequential with no rollback of the first if the second throws.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot the original bytes of every file the transaction touches, wrap :193-205 in try/catch, and restore on any failure; or write to a temp tree and rename in.

findings.area: stage modules — 21 focused-check commands point at tools that do not exist

findings.area: competing-guide detector — a real competing guide demonstrably evades it

verdicts:
NOT A CLEAN BILL OF HEALTH — the central claim under review is substantially true but its headline measurements are false, and three classifications close gaps without evidence.

WHAT HOLDS. The replacement of the ~840-line hardcoded obligation literal with a filesystem-derived universe is real and is a genuine structural improvement: tools/canon-impact.mjs contains no expected-count constant, the universe comes from fs.readdirSync, the 16-case fixture test passes, adding a canon file under a matched root produces exactly one bounded orphan and names no unrelated stage, and `--check` exits 0 with 0 errors on merged master. NOTHING WAS PRUNED: work items went 124 -> 125 with zero removals, all 16 stages (M0-M14 + FUTURE) and 18 modules survive, and I traced every one of the ten required topics — M0-M14, future-gated, federation, two-sovereign, connected/secured services, optional L1, embodiment, assurance, marketplaces, economics — to a named stage, work item and canon-map entry. The 10 pre-refactor root files absent by basename are 7-12-line pointer stubs whose bodies are archived; the one substantial file (58 PG-* gate registry) survives verbatim as modules/mechanism-gates.md. The 55 hand-curated canon-map entries and the 6 unresolved_canon_gap findings are outstanding work — deeply researched, code-verified, and several explicitly declare their own coverage as PARTIAL rather than inflating it.

WHAT DOES NOT HOLD.
1. BLOCKER — docs/evidence is 100% invisible. The retained_evidence rule matches zero files because walk() never emits directories and docs/evidence has no depth-0 files. Thirteen files are outside the universe, including program-control-source.json, pg-gate-map.json (all 58 PG-* ids), release-ladder.json and blocker-ledger.json, which five work items cite as evidence. The code contradicts its own justifying comment ("The directory itself is classified once" — it is not), and the bounding rationale ("per-run artifacts... proving nothing") does not describe program-control sources. The generated projection asserts docs/evidence coverage anyway (canon-impact.v1.json:47).
2. BLOCKER — conformance_only is an automatic gap-to-pass conversion in code (bootstrap-canon-map.mjs:211-218) whose stated proof is a documentation lint's exit code, applied to 16 targets including physical-action-safety and attestation-assurance. This is the brief's explicitly forbidden proof.
3. MAJOR — MEASUREMENTS.md:53 claims "445 subjects, 223 requiring explicit classification" against a shipped 432/210, and MEASUREMENTS.md:55 claims "Canon files invisible in every role: After 0" against an actual 13. The one claim I was asked to test hardest is false as stated.
4. MAJOR — a canon file that no rule matches is trivial to construct. I proved it in a scratch fixture: 8 of 10 plausible canon files were invisible, including any file in a new docs/ subdirectory, any .json under docs/specs|security|crypto, and any non-4-digit or nested ADR. The self-test writes fixture canon only to rule-matching paths, so it structurally cannot catch this class. Unmatched paths fail OPEN, not closed.
5. MAJOR — 155 of 210 classifications are nominal: mechanically derived from which work items already cited the path, with reasons literally reading "cited by N work item(s) in stage(s) X". foundations/invariants.md (INV-1..INV-36) is actively_sequenced with 30 work items and zero evidence, proof gates, conformance targets or code anchors, while PLAN.md:128 records its coverage as "closed". A FUTURE-stage, conditional_future fault-injection PLAN is recorded as an owning work item for 38 canon subjects including agentgres and wallet-network doctrine.
6. MAJOR — canon-to-code-delta.md, the densest statement of build obligation in the repo, is classified "states no build obligation of its own"; runtime-action-schema.json and legacy-ref-scheme-aliases.json are stripped of obligation status by a filename regex despite generating and gating live code; and canon-map asserts non_build_doctrine for exactly the two _meta files canon-gaps records as an open canon-owner question.
7. MAJOR — canon-gaps.v1.json:22 contains a factually false claim (authority-gateway-coverage is present at sequence.v1.json:568-569 and pulled at :222), disproved by the estate's own module-orphan checker.

BOTTOM LINE. Orphan DETECTION is now honest for the ~97% of docs/ the rules happen to cover. Coverage QUALITY is not: for three-quarters of subjects it is a restatement of citations the estate already held, "0 gaps" was achieved by reclassifying all 54 mechanically-detected gaps rather than by implementation, and the number the report leads with (445/223, 0 invisible) is not the number the tool produces (432/210, 13 invisible). Fix items 1, 2 and 3 before this estate is presented as covering docs/architecture end to end.

CHANGES REQUIRED — 1 BLOCKER, 7 MAJOR. The structural core of the refactor is real and largely holds up: root is genuinely 2 files, 621 markdown links and 589 canon-owner paths all resolve, the three role files are unique, front matter and status-voice discipline pass on every module I sampled, the 0.10s/0.48s lane timings reproduce exactly, the 58 PG-* gates survived intact, the 432→210 canon subject split is a legitimate attachment model rather than a silent pruning, and every planned/actively_sequenced subject provably binds to a real stage and a real work item. M1-ahead-of-M0 is surfaced as a blocker rather than buried, and the tracked-side changes are honestly scoped at 43 insertions / 0 deletions, uncommitted. The BLOCKER is that the refactor reproduced the precise defect it was chartered to eliminate: 45 references to 12 deleted tools are spread across 9 stage modules under "Focused checks during development", nine of them introduced by stages/m0.md:116 — the CURRENT stage — with the word "Verified", two lines above a paragraph criticising the retired master guide for exactly this. No checker validates commands, because check-estate.mjs's link bar only matches markdown link syntax and never inspects inline code. MEASUREMENTS.md:47 asserts "every command in a stage module is checked to exist"; no such check exists. The MAJOR findings cluster into two themes. First, enforcement that passes without testing anything: check-program.mjs discards sub-bar warnings and SKIPs and prints a fabricated "0 error, 0 warn, 0 skip" while check-no-competing-guides emits 4 warns and a SKIP whose own text reads "SKIP is not success" — a direct violation of rules.md §6; and that same competing-guide check passes vacuously because 39 of 102 registry paths, including all 5 classified active-implementation-guidance, are absent from the refactor's checkout while existing undemoted in the user's real one (I verified this directly), so the brief's "only first-party location with active guidance" requirement is not met and D12 is reproduced at 27→39. Second, claims that outrun the artifact: MEASUREMENTS.md:57's headline honesty metric of "55 missing_implementation_coverage, each named" is zero in the delivered canon map; the 150-line reader path omits the stage module that README.md:9 makes step 2 of its own path (real path 541 lines); and subject counts, file counts, and the 190-line stage-module ceiling (m13.md is 215) are all drifted. Separately, NOW.md publishes each record's out_of_scope verbatim, and that field duplicates nonclaims in 123 of 126 records — for the cut NOW.md named when this review began, it listed the cut's core deliverable as out of scope. That data defect is inherited verbatim from the pre-refactor estate, not created here, but the refactor promoted it onto the primary orientation surface without validating it.
